v2 vs v1 shows a clean change with an honest explanation: retrieving three documents instead of one lifted `retrieval_recall_at_3` from {{cmp.v2.retrieval_recall_at_3.baseline|.4f}} to {{cmp.v2.retrieval_recall_at_3.candidate|.4f}} and `retrieval_mrr_at_3` from {{cmp.v2.retrieval_mrr_at_3.baseline|.4f}} to {{cmp.v2.retrieval_mrr_at_3.candidate|.4f}}, both significant in the paired bootstrap, with {{cmp.v2.summary.verdict}} ({{cmp.v2.summary.n_improved}} improved, {{cmp.v2.summary.n_neutral}} neutral, {{cmp.v2.summary.n_inconclusive}} inconclusive). The success rate rose from {{cmp.v2.success_rate.baseline|.4f}} to {{cmp.v2.success_rate.candidate|.4f}}, but McNemar's test on the discordant cases gives p = {{cmp.v2.success_rate.p_value|.1g}}, so the gate reports it as inconclusive instead of crediting it. `retrieval_recall_at_1` did not move, and the ablation in `results/retrieval_ablation.json` shows that at equal K plain overlap weighting is at least as good as idf on this corpus (recall@3 {{abl.retrievers.overlap.recall_at_3|.4f}} vs {{abl.retrievers.idf.recall_at_3|.4f}}), so the gain is K, not idf. v3 vs v1 shows the interesting case: the fluent style keeps v2's retrieval but drops every citation, so `groundedness` falls from {{cmp.v3.groundedness.baseline|.1f}} to {{cmp.v3.groundedness.candidate|.1f}}, `gold_citation_recall` from {{cmp.v3.gold_citation_recall.baseline|.4f}} to {{cmp.v3.gold_citation_recall.candidate|.1f}} and `success_rate` from {{cmp.v3.success_rate.baseline|.4f}} to {{cmp.v3.success_rate.candidate|.4f}}, `citation_precision` disappears, and `ungrounded` failures rise by {{cmp.v3.fail.ungrounded}}. The regression report surfaces the retrieval-versus-grounding trade-off as separate rows instead of hiding it behind a single score: a composite might have netted v3 out as "fine".
